sentences.text: Rule thirty-five covers sound signals in or near an area of restricted visibility, by day or night.
Underway, signals are sounded at intervals of not more than two minutes.
A power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds one prolonged blast.
A power-driven vessel underway but stopped sounds two prolonged blasts, with about two seconds between them.
A vessel not under command, restricted, constrained by her draft, sailing, engaged in fishing, or towing or pushing sounds one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts.
A vessel towed, or the last vessel of a tow, if manned, sounds one prolonged followed by three short blasts, right after the towing vessel’s signal if practicable.
A composite pushing unit gives the signals of a power-driven vessel.
